design_rationale:
WORKLOG / DOSSIER — task 0 of private_homeflood_rating_billing (HomeFlood rating and billing), env_0065.

1. Draw and scope. draw_counts.py --task 0 printed {"prerequisite_problems": 3, "factor_counts": [6, 6, 4, 6]}. Task 0 claims four extended policies, the first claims of the difficulty: homeflood_ext_certificate_rerate (6 factors, agent tool apply_certificate_review_8d563756, subject homeflood_ec_received + homeflood_rating_updated), homeflood_ext_rerate_credit (4 factors, agent tool book_rerate_credit_70dc8da2, subject homeflood_premium_credit), homeflood_ext_renewal_booking (6 factors, agent tool book_renewal_term_27983a73, subject homeflood_term_renewed) and the root homeflood_ext_installment_payment (6 factors, owner=user tool pay_installment_4d782e9d, subject homeflood_premium_payment). Left for task 1 (draw 1 prerequisite, factors [5, 5]): the cancellation and closing-payment events (homeflood_policy_cancelled, CANCELLATION credits, a final payment) — an independent sale story with its own two policies; no policy, tool or event write of task 0 is reused there.

2. Why it is a good test. Nora Lindqvist only asks to pay her next quarterly installment early by ACH. The figure she must be quoted cannot be read anywhere: the 2026-09-01 renewal was paid (2026-08-14 deposit 806.52) but never booked, and an Elevation Certificate received 2026-07-20 sits with a re-rated premium of 0.00. The installment rule says an installment after the first is not fixed until its term carries its booked term premium item and only after every certificate entry received during an earlier term carries a RERATE credit, save one kept on file for the next term; the renewal rule says the renewal term premium is not fixed until every certificate entry received after the offer carries its re-rated premium, and the coming term is booked only after the expiring term carries its RERATE credit; the credit rule waits on the certificate entry carrying its re-rated premium. The agent must discover the chain review -> credit -> renewal -> installment from those state-form sentences and the records, then compute four multi-factor numbers on handling-time worlds.

3. Problem-tree card. Root homeflood_ext_installment_payment. Edges (all form=state): (a) rerate_credit -> certificate_rerate, value_input, gate new_premium, sentence "The re-rate credit is worked out only once the certificate entry carries its re-rated term premium in place of 0.00."; false at frozen_time: homeflood_changes[ec1].revised_term_premium = 0.0; only the certificate review writes that field. (b) renewal_booking -> certificate_rerate, value_input, gate cert_prem, sentence "The renewal term premium is not fixed until every Elevation Certificate entry received after the renewal offer carries its re-rated term premium in place of 0.00." (c) renewal_booking -> rerate_credit, state_gate, gate homeflood_billing.charge_basis, sentence "The coming term is booked only after every Elevation Certificate entry received during the expiring term carries a RERATE credit, save one kept on file for the next term with its re-rated term premium recorded."; false at frozen_time: the certificate entry recorded 2026-07-20 lies within the expiring term, is not kept on file (re-rated premium still 0.00) and no RERATE credit references it; only the re-rate credit write posts RERATE. (d) installment_payment -> renewal_booking, value_input, gate term_item, sentence "An installment after the first is not fixed until the term it belongs to carries its booked term premium item."; false: the installment's term is the term of the latest installment-1 payment (2026-08-14, term 2026-09-01) and no TERM_PREMIUM item carries term_start 2026-09-01; only the renewal booking books a renewal term premium item. (e) installment_payment -> rerate_credit, value_input, gate closed_credit, sentence "The installment due is fixed only after every Elevation Certificate entry received during an earlier term carries a RERATE credit, save one kept on file for the next term with its re-rated term premium recorded."; false at frozen_time for the same certificate entry Value-input edges 4 >= max(3-1,1). Directions are mixed (only after / not until / only once). Topological order, the only one: certificate_rerate (step 10) -> rerate_credit (12) -> renewal_booking (14) -> installment_payment (16). Deletion runs (scratch skip run): skip review -> credit 349.31 (vs 113.35), renewal 1,764.86 (vs 1,256.86), installment 197.03; skip credit -> renewal unchanged 1,256.86 but no RERATE row, installment 149.21; skip renewal -> installment 0.00 (no TERM_PREMIUM item on the installment's term; the result floors at zero). user_scenario names no prerequisite; it mentions the July certificate only if asked. No tool reads a prerequisite state (see tools_do_not_block).

4. Base-invariant card. apply_certificate_review: homeflood_ec_rating.ec_midterm_status ("A certificate is applied mid-term only on a policy whose status is pending_effective or active.") — homeflood_policies[hf].status = active at the review; homeflood_credits policy_scope. book_rerate_credit: ec_rating, endorsements, cancellation_refund, insurer_notices govern premium_credit, no gate applies (policy_scope). book_renewal_term: agg_property_combination, premium_rating, credits, renewal — gates apply only to issue/reinstatement (policy_scope); the renewal condition "first payment of the coming term ... received on or before term_end" holds by billing[dep26] posted 2026-08-14 <= 2026-09-01. pay_installment: payment_plans (gates apply only to rescission). No time gate applies; temporal_feasibility is empty.

5. Business-object card. Target: HomeFlood policy HF-3207461 (one HomeFlood policy for the customer). Certificate: the only homeflood_ec_received entry (ec1). Fall measured from the 2026-02-10 DEDUCTIBLE_INCREASE endorsement's 2,033.47 (the 2,244.01 TERM_PREMIUM item and the 2,244.01 offer for 2025 are excluded by the rule's order). The installment counts payments by term_start: 2025-09-01 term (4 ACH payments, balance 0.00 before the credit) vs 2026-09-01 term (deposit 806.52). Earlier-term credit = all-terms balance less current-term balance.

6. Factor cards (expected / tier / evidence / baseline figure):
certificate_rerate 1,373.62: elev_survey_age method (survey 2026-07-08, 0 months before 2026-07-20 receipt, diff 0 -> row 1.0; baseline 1.25 -> 1,705.77); vent_openings (openings, diff >= 0 -> 5; -> 1,449.97); loss_history cross dwelling multi-source (HomeFlood 4,420.00 inside 120 months, outside 36; NFIP 2012 loss outside both; denied 2020 NFIP claim -> 5; -> 1,449.97); excess_layer cross excess (XF-3409126 in force on 2025-09-01, limit 300,000 -> 3; -> 1,419.43); occupancy_use cross dwelling (primary residence -> 0.95; -> 1,443.54); nfip_transfer cross dwelling (159 months -> 0.96; -> 1,428.97). Whole baseline 2,138.12.
rerate_credit 113.35: credit_start_anchor method (received 2026-07-20, more than 30 days after the 2025-09-01 term start, survey after term start -> 2026-07-08, 55 days; baseline receipt 43 days -> 88.62); fall_measure_source method (latest endorsement recorded within the term -> 2,033.47; baseline item 2,244.01 -> 149.52); review_delay (92 days -> 4%; -> 109.37); vent_survey_addition (openings certified, surveyed 0 whole months before receipt -> 10%; -> 103.41). Whole baseline 102.54.
renewal_booking 1,256.86: start_figure_source method (certificate re-rate after the offer -> 1,373.62; baseline offer 1,928.81 -> 1,764.86); early_renewal (18 days -> 1.5; -> 1,277.47); payment_history (1 notice -> +3; -> 1,215.65); tenure_loyalty cross dwelling (209 months -> 5; -> 1,325.54); household_policy cross dwelling+excess (in-force NFIP condo on a non-primary residence and active Excess at the HomeFlood address -> 3; -> 1,298.07); autopay_history (4 ACH -> 2; -> 1,284.33). Whole baseline 1,928.81.
installment_payment 111.43: deposit_spread method (overpaid 268.776 over 3 -> -89.592; -> 201.02); earlier_term_credit method (113.35 over 3 -> -37.783; -> 149.21); autopay_fee (0; baseline 6 -> 117.43); pay_ahead (1 month -> 1%; -> 113.94); booking_delay (49 days -> 3%; -> 118.97); excess_paid_up cross excess (active, balance 0 -> 1%; -> 113.94). Whole baseline 257.37.
Near-misses: the 2023-08-30 HomeFlood loss is 37 months back (outside the 36-month window), the 2012 NFIP loss is 171 months back (outside 120), the 2020 NFIP claim was denied; the 2025-08-27 ACH payment is 13 months back (outside the 12-month fee window); the 2026-02-10 endorsement lies before the 2026-07-03 offer, so it is not a renewal start figure. Stale stamps: policy credits_applied_pct 5, excess_package true and ec_on_file false are not read by any rule.

7. Factor independence (checked by reading compute): no factor binding reads another factor's binding. Shared plain bindings: cert_received/cert_survey/cert_bfe/cert_diff, nfip_id, nfip_orig (certificate_rerate); cert_received, cert_survey, new_premium, hf_cert_count, term_days, pro_rata (rerate_credit); offer_prem (renewal_booking); share_pct, down_pct, planned, term_item, share, paid_count, remaining, prev_due_months (installment). Results are assembled only in result/credit_pct/net_pct. Method tier pairs: elev (non-SFHA vs fresh: zone; fresh vs aged: survey age 59 vs 61 months; aged vs otherwise: age 125 months); credit start (earlier entry vs survey: entry count; survey vs receipt: survey before/after term start); fall source (endorsement within the term vs offer: endorsement date; offer vs item: offer present); start figure (certificate re-rated after offer vs endorsement after offer: certificate premium 0.00 or not; endorsement vs offer: endorsement date vs offer date); deposit (3+ vs 1-2 vs 0 still to come); earlier credit (QUARTERLY 2+ vs SEMI/1 vs none).

8. Edge probes (probe0.py on scratch copies of the world, certificate re-rate): older decoy certificate entry -> 1,373.62 (latest used); no certificate -> 1,801.22 (no-EC 1.25); no NFIP record -> 1,501.82 (occupancy/transfer 1, insured months from 2022-09-01 = 49, loss tier claims_free 5 because the only HomeFlood loss is 37 months back); no Excess -> 1,419.43; Excess closed after term start -> 1,419.43 (since round 4 only the active Excess Flood policy at the address is read, so a closed one earns no layer credit); Excess effective after term start -> 1,419.43; survey 85 months old -> 1,905.06 (row for difference less one foot); survey older than 120 months -> 1,801.22 (no-EC factor and, since round 2, no flood-vent credit from a certificate not accepted for rating); no BFE -> 1,667.59 (vent 10, no-EC). Known first-match limits: one NFIP record per address and one Excess policy per address are assumed by the rules ("the customer's ... at the address").

9. Persona. Brisk retired teacher; volunteers only the goal (pay the next installment today, by ACH), gives phone then SSN last four only when asked, agrees passively when told something must be put right first, answers about the July certificate and other policies only if asked, makes the payment herself when handed the tool, ends on confirmation.

10. Standard solution and verification. Reads: find_customers(phone) -> verify (phone + 3618) -> find_homeflood_policies -> changes -> billing -> claims -> find_dwelling_policies -> find_dwelling_claims(nfip) -> find_excess_policies. Writes: apply_certificate_review(revised 1,373.62, credits 13, ec_applied true) -> book_rerate_credit(113.35) -> book_renewal_term(1,256.86, fee 35.0) -> hand over pay_installment(111.43, installment 2, ACH). Verification: scratch sim.py replays the real tools and evaluates compute with check_compute's own evaluator; outputs equal computations.expected; gates run: check_extended/task_tools/replay/solvability/compute/grounding/cross_fire --task 0 all OK.

11. Draft visible-context recomputation. From the rule prose (published as hub, baseline and factor documents), the tool schemas and lookup returns alone, the same order follows (each sentence names a record state only one write produces), and each figure is reproduced from the rows listed in the read nodes; no hidden asset is needed.

REWORK round 2 (audit F2, F3, F4, T0-C1, T0-C2, T0-T1, T0-T2, observations O1-O5). (1) 'The re-rating date' is now defined in the certificate rule as the day the review is completed and recorded (not the receipt date, not the term start); all loss-history windows and the tenure count end on that day, so the reading that anchors the lookback on 2026-07-20 or 2025-09-01 is excluded; the booking date (renewal), the payment date (installment) are defined the same way. (2) The two edges on the re-rate credit now quantify over certificate entries received during the expiring / an earlier term, excluding only one kept on file for the next term with its re-rated premium recorded; the 2026-07-20 entry (re-rated premium 0.00) is therefore an unmet member at the opening, not a vacuous set. (3) The installment's term is defined as the term of the latest installment-1 payment, and every installment binding (term item, payments, pay-ahead, booking delay) reads that term; term_item is 0.00 at the opening and 1,256.86 after the renewal booking, as the edge declares. (4) Seed: claim 3HF2300871 now pays 4,420.00 (ACV 6,420.00 less the 2,000 deductible in force in 2023, because 350,000 < 80% of 680,000), a figure the base settlement rule produces; the loss-history tier is unchanged (net payment above zero inside 120 months, outside 36). (5) Proof text: the pro rata of the re-rate credit is 99.4295; the 'no NFIP record' probe gives the claims-free tier 5 (1,501.82). (6) Observations closed: the flood-vent credit now requires an accepted certificate (probe: survey older than 120 months -> 1,801.22); the renewal's early-renewal credit reads the coming term's installment-1 payment; the earlier-term credit is stated as the earlier terms taken together; the booking-delay credit is nothing when no term premium item is booked. All four scored values and every factor_sensitivity figure were recomputed after the changes and are unchanged (1,373.62 / 113.35 / 1,256.86 / 111.43).

REWORK round 3 (renderer source scan render_r1: M2, M3, M5, M6, ties, placement). Overwrite tails now restate the still-in-force base content for every out-of-scope case instead of pointing at the base rule. The household credit now reads the existence of an in-force NFIP policy on a non-primary residence plus an active Excess Flood policy at the HomeFlood address (no first-match pick among NFIP policies); this world takes the same 3% tier. The review-delay addition counts to the day the re-rate credit is booked (the day the review counts as completed). The pay-ahead count is stated exactly as computed (whole months from the term start less the previous due month offset). Same-day ties (first recorded counts) and the nearest-cent rounding with halves to even are stated in every rule; the credit-start tiers were at that round worded on 'another certificate entry' (replaced in round 5 by receipt-date tiers). Single-factor definitions moved into their factors (NFIP id and re-rating date -> loss history; survey date -> credit start; previous-due offset -> pay-ahead; NFIP record -> loyalty). Absent-record tiers added (no coming-term first payment; no first payment for the installment). All scored values and factor_sensitivity figures recomputed unchanged.

REWORK round 4 (audit revision_3: R3-3 members 1-4). Every first-record-by-address read now has an exact scope: the NFIP record (certificate re-rate: loss history, occupancy, NFIP transfer; renewal: loyalty) is the NFIP policy this HomeFlood policy replaced, read by its policy number (the policy's replaced NFIP policy number); the layer credit and the Excess paid-up credit read the Excess Flood policy in status active at the address, unique by the Excess Flood program's one-live-policy-per-address rule. The NFIP transfer condition no longer re-tests the number. The installment's deposit is the payments received for the term as its installment 1; the early-renewal credit reads the latest payment received for the coming term as its installment 1. Adversarial probe sweep at all four handling times (cancelled earlier Excess at the address listed first, second in-force NFIP record at the HomeFlood address listed first, cancelled primary NFIP elsewhere, paid-then-voided payment on a new claim, older renewal offer for an earlier term): every scored value unchanged; a same-day second certificate entry recorded after the one under review leaves the re-rate unchanged (first recorded counts); at round 4 it moved the re-rate credit's start to the term start through the 'another certificate entry' tier, which round 5 replaced. All scored values and factor_sensitivity figures recomputed unchanged.

REWORK round 5 (KB audit source items S1-S5). S1: the certificate re-rate now declares the overwrite of the base clause 'The total credit percent from the credit rule then reduces the result.'; its replacement is the re-rate's own credit assembly, and the baseline says outright that the credit percent recorded on the policy for the term is not carried into the re-rating (one reading: the whole baseline stays the no-credit figure). S2: 'Excess Flood program' replaces the authoring word. S3: certificate acceptance in the re-rate rests on the recorded survey and receipt dates, the entry being recorded only for a FEMA-form, sealed certificate of an unaltered building. S4: the two autopay ladders say 'one to three payments, every one by ACH' (zero payments fall through), matching the compute. S5: the cancellation rule no longer restates the closing payment's fee table. Count-keyed tiers removed from the re-rate credit: the credit start's first tier now keys on the receipt date (received before or within 30 days after the term start -> from the term start) and the former first-certificate addition is a mitigation-survey addition keyed on the certificate under review (openings certified; surveyed fewer than 3 whole months before receipt -> 10%, older survey -> 5%); this world takes the same tiers and figures. All scored values and factor_sensitivity figures recomputed unchanged. Round 5 also: the fall source's first tier is the latest endorsement entry recorded within the term (every endorsement entry carries the full-term premium in force as endorsed, so a later no-premium endorsement no longer switches the source); the re-rate credit is capped at the net premium booked for the term (TERM_PREMIUM and ENDORSEMENT_PREMIUM items less ENDORSEMENT and RERATE credits; 2,126.91 here, not binding). Probes: an older endorsement in a prior term, a mortgagee change recorded after receipt, and a same-day second certificate leave the credit unchanged. Round 6 (R5-1, T0-R5-1): the fall source's first tier now bounds 'within the term' on both sides in rule and compute (on or after term_start and before term_end); the stale tier_taken of that factor is corrected. Values unchanged.

REWORK round 7 (KB cross-product re-judge S6, S7; seed only). Excess XF-3409126 now carries the term premium the Excess rate manual produces for Excess Flood 500K at a 300,000 layer in zone AE with no certificate (300,000 / 1,000 x 1.55 = 465.00, zone 1.0, no elevation credit, plus loss-of-use 110.00 = 575.00, raised to the 650.00 minimum) and the standalone 30-day wait (application 2024-02-26 -> effective 2024-03-27, renewal term 2026-03-27 to 2027-03-27); it still took effect before the 2025-09-01 term start, is active with a zero balance, so the layer, household and Excess paid-up credits are unchanged. The NFIP condominium policy 3118840265 now shows application 2018-02-08 (30-day standard wait to the 2018-03-10 original effective date) and no ICC premium (ICC does not attach on the Residential Condominium Unit tier); only its status and primary-residence flag are read. All scored values unchanged.
user_scenario: You are Nora Lindqvist, a retired schoolteacher in St. Petersburg, Florida, calling Tidemark about the HomeFlood flood policy on your home at 336 Brightwaters Blvd NE. You are flying out in early November to spend the winter with your daughter in Minnesota, and you want to pay your next flood installment today so that nothing falls due while you are away. You speak plainly and a little briskly, like someone working down a to-do list. You have always paid this policy by bank transfer and want to pay this one the same way, by ACH from your usual checking account. You do not know what the next installment comes to and you do not guess at it; you expect the representative to tell you the amount, and you will pay exactly the amount and installment they give you. You do not remember the policy number. When the representative wants to confirm who you are, you give your phone number, 3055531847; if they ask for one more detail you give the last four digits of your Social Security number, 3618, and if they ask for your ZIP code it is 33704. If the representative tells you that something else on the account has to be put right or booked before the installment can be worked out, you say that is fine and to go ahead and do whatever they need on their end, and you wait while they do it. Only if the representative asks about an Elevation Certificate do you mention that your surveyor sent one to Tidemark in July, after the flood vents were put in, and that you assumed Tidemark had it; you know nothing about how it is rated. Only if they ask whether you have other policies with Tidemark do you say you also have the excess flood policy on this house and a federal flood policy on a rental condo in Indian Rocks Beach. When the representative hands the payment over for you to make yourself, you make it by ACH for the amount and installment number they quoted, and you repeat the payment reference if they ask for it. Once the payment has gone through and you hear it confirmed, you thank them and say goodbye.

prerequisite_closure.order_uniqueness: There is a single topological order: the re-rate credit depends on the certificate review; the renewal booking depends on both the certificate review and the re-rate credit; the installment depends on the renewal booking and the re-rate credit. No two problems are left unordered, so no commuting proof is needed; the edge renewal booking -> re-rate credit also keeps the credit on the 2025-09-01 term, because the renewal booking moves the policy's term dates.

edge_load_bearing.skipped_effect: without the certificate review the re-rate credit is computed with a re-rated premium of 0.00: 349.31 instead of 113.35 (prerequisite-sensitivity run).
renewal_term_premium starts from the offered 1,928.81: 1,764.86 instead of 1,256.86.
state gate: renewal_term_premium is unchanged (1,256.86) but the terminal ledger lacks the RERATE credit row on the 2025-09-01 term and the installment becomes 149.21 instead of 111.43.

with no TERM_PREMIUM item on the installment's term (2026-09-01) term_item stays 0.00, the share and the deposit base vanish and the installment floors at 0.00 instead of 111.43 (prerequisite-sensitivity run).
with no RERATE credit there is no earlier-term credit to spread: 149.21 instead of 111.43.

prerequisite_closure.no_user_hint: user_scenario asks only to pay the next installment by ACH. It never mentions the certificate review, a re-rate credit or the renewal booking; the surveyor's July certificate is mentioned only if the representative asks about an Elevation Certificate, and agreement to 'put right or book' something is a passive reaction after the representative explains it. No policy id appears in it.
prerequisite_closure.tools_do_not_block: task_tools.py: book_rerate_credit_70dc8da2, book_renewal_term_27983a73 and pay_installment_4d782e9d only look up the policy row for its customer, term and balance and then ctx.create/ctx.update; none reads the certificate entry's re-rated premium, the RERATE credit or the term's TERM_PREMIUM item, and none returns an error when they are missing.
